text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President Hosni Mubarak and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat discuss issues to be negotiated in the transitional and final status stages and the need for precise implementation of the Hebron deal. Arafat says, after meeting Mubarak and Arab League Secretary General Esmat Abdel-Meguid, that there are still 34 unsolved points that the Palestinians hope to settle with the Israelis soon.
- Mubarak to chair the Middle East session at the Davos Forum on world economy later this month in Switzerland.

- Egypt will build the first power plant in the region to generate electricity by pumping water. The plant will pump and store water from the Red Sea up to the summit of Mt Ataqa, and then use it to generate electricity. Electricity Minister Maher Abaza says the plant will be set up next year on a BOT basis.

- Egypt watches the developments in Sudan, a diplomatic source says. Head of the Sudanese National Democratic Forum, Mohamed Osman al-Merghani, says the continuation of the Sudanese regime threatens the unity of Sudan.

- The cabinet discusses reports on the development of the South Valley and Sinai. Information Minister Safwat el-Sherif says the meeting approved several decisions, including the encouragement of private-sector investments.
- Mubarak confirms to Arafat that Egypt will continue its support to the Palestinians.
- The government to refer to parliament, within the coming days, a draft law on exempting investors in the new South Valley development project from taxes for 25 years.
